en.title: Eli Roth-Produced 'Burger Night' Casts All-Female Lead Trio
en.summary: An all-female trio has been tapped to lead the upcoming horror film 'Burger Night: Luli, Magda & Lore,' an Argentine spin-off from Joe Begos' 'Jimmy and Stiggs.' The project is executive produced by horror maestro Eli Roth.
en.body:
Get ready for a dose of Argentinian horror with **Eli Roth**’s latest production venture. **‘Burger Night: Luli, Magda & Lore’** has officially rounded out its main cast, announcing a trio of talented actresses ready to dive into the genre. The film is an Argentine spin-off of **Joe Begos**’ alien horror flick **‘Jimmy and Stiggs,’** and it’s set to bring a distinctively local flavor to the terror.

Leading the charge are **Agostina Palazzolo**, known for her work in **‘Ciclón,’** **Agustina “Papry” Suásquita**, who audiences might recognize from Netflix’s **‘Envious,’** and **Maia Tarcic**, who has appeared in **‘Letters to My Ex.’** Their collective presence promises a dynamic and potentially chilling performance as they navigate whatever horrors await them in **‘Burger Night.’** The involvement of **Grupo Morbido**’s **Pablo Guisa Koestinger** further solidifies the film’s genre credentials, suggesting a commitment to delivering authentic and impactful horror experiences.

## A Fresh Take on Terror

While the specifics of the plot remain under wraps, the premise of an Argentine spin-off from an alien horror film, now featuring an all-female lead cast and executive produced by **Eli Roth**, is certainly piqued our interest. Roth, a name synonymous with modern horror, has a knack for identifying and nurturing projects that push boundaries and deliver visceral thrills. His executive producer credit on **‘Burger Night’** suggests a hands-on approach and a belief in the vision of the filmmakers involved. This collaboration hints at a film that could blend familiar horror elements with a unique cultural perspective, potentially exploring themes and anxieties specific to its Argentinian setting.

The decision to center the narrative around an all-female cast is a significant and welcome development. In a genre that has historically, and sometimes problematically, portrayed women, a strong, female-driven horror story offers exciting possibilities. It opens the door for complex character development and a narrative that can subvert expectations, offering a powerful voice to its protagonists as they confront the unknown.

## What the Fans Can Expect

For fans of **Eli Roth**, **Joe Begos**, and international horror, **‘Burger Night’** represents a highly anticipated addition to the genre. The combination of a seasoned horror icon like Roth and the creative energy of an emerging Argentinian production team is a recipe for something special. The teaser hints at a narrative connected to alien horror, and the focus on a female-led ensemble suggests that this spin-off will forge its own identity, rather than simply rehashing the original. We can anticipate a film that is both terrifying and thought-provoking, delivering the kind of scares that Roth is known for, but with a fresh perspective.

The anticipation is palpable for more details to emerge about the specific nature of the horror and how the characters of Luli, Magda, and Lore will interact. The success of **‘Jimmy and Stiggs’** has already built a foundation for this universe, and **‘Burger Night’** has the potential to expand it in thrilling new directions. This is more than just another horror flick; it’s a statement about the evolving landscape of genre filmmaking and the diverse stories that deserve to be told.

## What's Next

Details regarding the production timeline, filming locations, and a release date for **‘Burger Night: Luli, Magda & Lore’** have not yet been announced. However, with the main cast now confirmed, audiences can expect further updates as the project moves closer to production. Keep an eye on WeCult News for more exclusive information as it becomes available.
